meta.title: Nuru · The first Swahili programming language
meta.description: Learn to program in Swahili. Draw with kobe, light up the ubao board, and run code in your browser with nothing to install.

landing.lead: Nuru is a programming language written in Swahili. You no longer translate an idea into English before you can write it down: you type `kama`, `wakati` and `andika`, words you already know.

card.label: A Nuru program being typed and run

items.title: Write in Swahili
items.body: Variables, decisions, loops and functions in words you know. Even the error messages speak Swahili.

items.title: Draw with Kobe
items.body: Steer the turtle with `mbele` and `kulia` and it draws shapes, stars and flowers on the canvas.

items.title: Light up Ubao
items.body: A simulated electronics board with 8 lights, a buzzer and a screen. Write hardware programs before you hold a real kit.

walimu.title: The whole class on one screen
walimu.body: Open a class in the Teachers' Room and get a join code. Learners sign in with the code, their name and a picture password. No email and no password, even when they share one phone.

steps.title: Open a class
steps.body: You get a short join code, like KJM-7Q4.

steps.title: Learners join
steps.body: Code, name and a picture password. That is all.

steps.title: Follow progress
steps.body: A live grid shows who has finished which lesson.

contributors.title: Built by a community
contributors.body: Nuru is open source. These people wrote its code, docs and lessons. You are welcome to join them.

mwisho.text: The first lesson takes five minutes.
mwisho.meaning: Nothing to install, no account needed. Open it and start.

footer.openSource: Nuru is open source. The code lives on GitHub.

kamusi.metaDescription: The complete Nuru language reference: variables, data types, decisions, loops, functions, modules and common errors, each with an example you can run.
kamusi.title: Kamusi ya Nuru
kamusi.lead: Every keyword, function and module in Nuru, each with an example you can run. The code stays in Swahili, as you will write it. Every example has been checked against the real Nuru.

ramani.title: Your Journey
ramani.lead: Each module is a stop on the journey. Finish its lessons, then move on.
ramani.savedHere: Your progress is saved on this device.
